source.title: Inner Speech: Development, Cognitive Functions, Phenomenology, and Neurobiology

confidence_rationale: The canonical integrative review of inner speech, explicitly built on the Vygotskian internalisation account (social speech -> private/egocentric speech -> condensed inner speech) and reporting the neurobiology (left inferior frontal gyrus / Broca's area as the production core; superior temporal gyrus involvement; supplementary motor and parietal contributions). It grounds MECH-380's central assertion -- that overt self-narration is the EXTERNAL phase of a cognitive-control system that later compresses inward -- with mechanism evidence rather than textbook analogy, and grounds MECH-381's compression ladder via the documented private->inner speech internalisation. Confidence held below 0.8 by the architectural-mapping step: the review describes inner speech as verbal thinking / self-monitoring / executive support, not as an arbitration-driving control surface in REE's specific sense, and REE has no spoken-language modality at all.
failure_signatures: The review documents that inner speech SUPPORTS executive function, planning, and self-regulation, but it does not establish that the external (overt) phase is functionally NECESSARY as a control surface -- the correlation between private-speech use and task performance is developmental and individual-difference evidence, not a demonstration that cognition must be externalised before it can be internalised.

Inner speech is shown to be variable (some adults report little; condensed vs expanded forms differ) -- the ladder MECH-381 asserts is a central tendency, not an obligatory sequence, which weakens any claim that the externalise-then-internalise route is the ONLY developmental path to internal control.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Inner speech (covert/verbal thinking) develops via Vygotskian internalisation -- external social speech is appropriated as private (egocentric) speech that regulates the child's own behaviour, then condenses into covert inner speech that retains a syntactically abbreviated, sometimes dialogic structure. It is implicated in executive function, planning, task-switching, and self-regulation, with a neurobiology centred on left inferior frontal gyrus (production) plus temporal and parietal regions.
mapping.ree_translation: Direct grounding for MECH-380 (private speech is the external phase of a cognitive-control system that makes regulation inspectable before it compresses) and MECH-381 (the externalise-then-internalise compression ladder). The neurobiology -- a dedicated production core (left IFG) whose output later runs covertly -- is the biological warrant for REE's proposed self-narration control surface and for the claim that the surface can become internal without losing its control function.
mapping.mapping_caveat: REE has no linguistic modality; the 'narration' in MECH-380/384 is a structured trace, not natural-language inner speech. The review grounds the DEVELOPMENTAL ARCHITECTURE (externalise -> internalise; a production core that goes covert) but not the specific claim that such a surface should DRIVE attention/action/affect arbitration -- that is REE's design commitment, beyond what the review demonstrates.
mapping.source_context: Integrative review across developmental psychology, cognitive neuroscience (fMRI/lesion), psycholinguistics, and atypical populations (children, AVH-experiencers); human only.

confidence_components.notes: Top-tier review venue, canonical and heavily cited; source quality high. Mapping fidelity moderate because the developmental architecture transfers but the control-surface-drives-arbitration step is REE's. Transfer risk elevated: human spoken/covert language -> a non-linguistic V4 substrate that does not yet exist.
